items.stem: Why require human confirmation before a voice agent writes a change to the CRM?

options.text: Speech recognition can mishear, so a person should confirm before committing
options.rationale: Correct: human confirmation guards against acting on misheard input.

options.text: Because the CRM cannot accept writes otherwise
options.rationale: The CRM can accept writes; the control is about safety.

options.text: Because confirmation speeds up the call
options.rationale: Confirmation adds a safety step, not speed.

items.explanation: Correct: human confirmation guards against acting on misheard input.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO belong in a supervised voice-service design? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A defined point at which the call escalates to a human
options.rationale: Correct: escalation handles cases beyond the agent's safe scope.

options.text: Consent and disclosure that the caller is speaking to an assistant
options.rationale: Correct: disclosure and consent are baseline requirements.
High-risk actions should not be unsupervised.

options.text: Launching to all callers with no pilot
options.rationale: A supervised pilot should precede full launch.

items.explanation: Correct: escalation handles cases beyond the agent's safe scope.

items.stem: A caller interrupts the agent mid-sentence. What must a realtime voice design handle?

options.text: Turn interruption, stopping the agent and listening to the caller
options.rationale: Correct: natural calls require handling interruptions gracefully.

options.text: Ignoring the caller until the agent finishes
options.rationale: Ignoring interruptions produces an unusable experience.

options.text: Ending the call on any interruption
options.rationale: Ending the call on interruption is not acceptable handling.

items.explanation: Correct: natural calls require handling interruptions gracefully.
